sentences.text:
OFFICE NO. NOTE  RNT,J  1. 11.09.2023  Learned counsel for the petitioners,
 A.P.S.R.T.C and its Depot Manager submits that the  respondent No.3, Hindupur Municipality vide letter Roc.No.1058/2021/G1, dated 14.11.2022, asked the petitioners to hand over the 20' feet wide piece of land, belonging to the petitioners for widening of the present 40' feet road from RTC DM Quarters to Cocoon market free of cost to Hindupur Municipality for constructing CC drain.
The petitioners submitted reply dated 16.11.2022 that the said land was owned by A.P.S.R.T.C and cannot be given for free.

Subsequently the Municipality submitted another letter Roc. No.
1058/2021/E1, dated 29.08.2023, informing about the Council's Resolution and plan of the proposed CC drain in A.P.S.R.T.C land for submitting to higher authorities and requested to take necessary action for laying of drain, otherwise the work will be taken up by the Department without further intimation.
2. Challenging the action of the Municipality, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that in view of Section 42 of the Andhra Pradesh SL. DATE ORDER OFFICE NO. NOTE Municipalities Act,
there is procedure for acquisition of immovable property by resorting to the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act and on payment of the compensation.

entities.text: Andhra Pradesh SL. DATE ORDER OFFICE NO. NOTE Municipalities Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. He further submits that under sub-section (2) of Section 42, if a municipal authority proposes to acquire any immovable property otherwise than under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act, he shall obtain the previous approval of the District Collector, upon which the District Collector shall proceed as per the said provision.
4. He submits that it is evident from the letters of the Municipality, that it is admitting the property to be of the A.P.S.R.T.C, but is asking for free.
The proceedings for acquisition under the Land Acquisition Act have not been initiated nor any approval of the District Collector have been obtained.

The action of the Municipality is contrary to the provisions of Section 42 of the Municipality Act and is also violative of the petitioners' right to property under Article 300-A of the Constitution of India.
5. Learned Standing Counsel for the respondent No.3 and learned Government Pleader for Municipal Administration for the respondent Nos.1 and 2, seek time to obtain instructions.
